source_text: Ὅτι δὲ Μωϋσῆς εἶπεν: Οὐ φάγεσθε χοῖρον οὔτε ἀετὸν οὔτε ὀξύπτερον οὔτε κόρακα οὔτε πάντα ἰχθύν, ὃς οὐκ ἔχει λεπίδα ἐν ἑαυτῷ, τρία ἔλαβεν ἐν τῇ συνέσει δόγματα. πέρας γέ τοι λέγει αὐτοῖς ἐν τῷ Δευτερονομίῳ: Καὶ διαθήσομαι πρὸς τὸν λαὸν τοῦτον τὰ δικαιώματά μου. ἄρα οὖν οὐκ ἔστιν ἐντολὴ θεοῦ τὸ μὴ τρώγειν, Μωϋσῆς δὲ ἐν πνεύματι ἐλάλησεν. τὸ οὖν χοιρίον πρὸς τοῦτο εἶπεν: οὐ κολληθήσῃ φησίν, ἀνθρώποις τοιούτοις, οἵτινές εἰσιν ὅμοιοι χοίρων: τουτέστιν ὅταν σπαταλῶσιν, ἐπιλανθάνονται τοῦ κυρίου, ὅταν δὲ ὑστεροῦνται, ἐπιγινώσκουσιν τὸν κύριον, ὡς καὶ ὁ χοῖρος ὅταν τρώγει τὸν κύριον οὐκ οἶδεν, ὅταν δὲ πεινᾷ κραυγάζει, καὶ λαβὼν πάλιν σιωπᾷ. Οὐδὲ φάγῃ τὸν ἀετὸν οὐδὲ τὸν ὀξύπτερον οὐδὲ τὸν ἰκτῖνα οὐδὲ τὸν κόρακα: οὐ μή, φησίν, κολληθήσῃ οὐδὲ ὁμοιωθήσῃ ἀνθρώποις τοιούτοις, οἵτινες οὐκ οἴδασιν διὰ κόπου καὶ ἱδρῶτος πορίζειν ἑαυτοῖς τὴν τροφήν, ἀλλὰ ἁρπάζουσιν τὰ ἀλλότρια ἐν ἀνομίᾳ αὐτῶν καὶ ἐπιτηροῦσιν ὡς ἐν ἀκεραιοσύνῃ περιπατοῦντες καὶ περιβλέπονται, τίνα ἐκδύσωσιν διὰ τὴν πλεονεξίαν, ὡς καὶ τὰ ὄρνεα ταῦτα μόνα ἑαυτοῖς οὐ προίζει τὴν τροφήν, ἀλλὰ ἀργὰ καθήμενα ἐκζητεῖ, πῶς ἀλλοτρίας σάρκας καταφάγῃ, ὄντα λοιμὰ τῇ πονηρίᾳ αὐτῶν. Καὶ οὐ φάγῃ, φησίν, σμύραιναν οὐδὲ πολύποδα οὐδὲ σηπίαν: οὐ μή, φησίν, ὁμοιωθήσῃ κολλώμενος ἀνθρώποις τοιούτοις, οἵτινες εἰς τέλος εἰσὶν ἀσεβεῖς καὶ κεκριμένοι ἤδη τῷ θανάτῳ, ὡς καὶ ταῦτα τὰ ἰχθύδια μόνα ἐπικατάρατα ἐν τῷ βυθῷ νήχεται, μὴ κολυμβῶντα ὡς τὰ λοιπά, ἀλλ’ ἐν τῇ γῇ κάτω τοῦ βυθοῦ κατοικεῖ. ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸν δασύποδα οὐ φάγῃ. πρὸς τί; οὐ μὴ γένῃ, φησίν, παιδοφθόρος οὐδὲ ὁμοιωθήσῃ τοῖς τοιούτοις, ὅτι ὁ λαγωὸς κατ’ ἐνιαυτὸν πλεονεκτεῖ τὴν ἀφόδευσιν: ὅσα γὰρ ἔτη ζῇ, τοσαύτας ἔχει τρύπας. ἀλλὰ οὐδὲ τὴν ὕαιναν φάγῃ: οὐ μή, φησίν, γένῃ μοιχὸς οὐδὲ φθορεὺς οὐδὲ ὁμοιωθήσῃ τοῖς τοιούτοις. πρὸς τί; ὅτι τὸ ζῷον τοῦτο παρ ἐνιαυτὸν ἀλλάσσει τὴν φύσιν καὶ ποτὲ μὲν ἄρρεν, ποτὲ δὲ θῆλυ γίνεται. ἀλλὰ καὶ τὴν γαλῆν ἐμίσησεν καλῶς. οὐ μή, φησίν, γενηθῇς τοιοῦτος, οἵους ἀκούομεν ἀνομίαν ποιοῦντας ἐν τῷ στόματι δἰ ἀκαθαρσίαν, οὐδὲ κολληθήσῃ ταῖς ἀκαθάρτοις ταῖς τὴν ἀνομίαν ποιούσαις ἐν τῷ στόματι. τὸ γὰρ ζῷον τοῦτο τῷ στόματι κύει. περὶ μὲν τῶν βρωμάτων λαβὼν Μωϋσῆς τρία δόγματα οὕτως ἐν πνεύματι ἐλάλησεν: οἱ δὲ κατ’ ἐπιθυμίαν τῆς σαρκὸς ὡς περὶ βρώσεως προσεδέξαντο. λαμβάνει δὲ τῶν αὐτῶν τριῶν δογμάτων γνῶσιν Δαυείδ καὶ λέγει: Μακάριος ἀνήρ, ὃς οὐκ ἐπορεύθη ἐν βουλῇ ἀσεβῶν, καθὼς καὶ οἱ ἰχθύες πορεύονται ἐν σκότει εἰς τὰ βάθη: καὶ ἐν ὁδῷ ἁμαρτωλῶν οὐκ ἔστη, καθὼς οἱ δοκοῦντες φοβεῖσθαι τὸν κύριον ἁμαρτάνουσιν ὡς ὁ χοῖρος, καὶ ἐπὶ καθέδραν λοιμῶν οὐκ ἐκάθισεν, καθὼς τὰ πετεινὰ καθήμενα εἰς ἁρπαγήν. ἔχετε τελείως καὶ περὶ τῆς βρώσεως. πάλιν λέγει Μωϋσῆς: Φάγεσθε πᾶν διχηλοῦν καὶ μαρυκώμενον. τί λέγει; ὅτι τὴν τροφὴν λαμβάνων οἶδεν τὸν τρέφοντα αὐτὸν καὶ ἐπ’ αὐτῷ ἀναπαυόμενος εὐφραίνεσθαι δοκεῖ. καλῶς εἶπεν βλέπων τὴν ἐντολήν. τί οὖν λέγει; κολλᾶσθε μετὰ τῶν φοβουμένων τὸν κύριον, μετὰ τῶν μελετώντων ὃ ἔλαβον διάσταλμα ῥήματος ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ, μετὰ τῶν λαλούντων τὰ διδαιώματα κυρίου καὶ τηρούντων, μετὰ τῶν εἰδότων, ὅτι ἡ μελέτη ἐστὶν ἔργον εὐφροσύνης, καὶ ἀναμαρυκωμένων τὸν λόγον κυρίου. τί δὲ τὸ διχηλοῦν; ὅτι ὁ δίκαιος καὶ ἐν τούτῳ τῷ κόσμῳ περιπατεῖ καὶ τὸν ἅγιον αἰῶνα ἐκδέχεται. βλέπετε, πῶς ἐνομοθέτησεν Μωϋσῆς καλῶς. ἀλλὰ πόθεν ἐκείνοις ταῦτα νοῆσαι ἢ συνιέναι; ἡμεῖς δὲ δικαίως νοήσαντες τὰς ἐντολὰς λαλοῦμεν, ὡς ἠθέλησεν ὁ κύριος. διὰ τοῦτο περιέτεμεν τὰς ἀκοὰς ἡμῶν καὶ τὰς καρδίας, ἵνα συνιῶμεν ταῦτα.
pass_a_gloss: For Moses said: You will not eat pig nor eagle nor oxypecter nor crow nor all fish which does not have scale in itself, he took three doctrines in wisdom. For he says to them in Deuteronomy: And I will make a covenant with this people my righteous deeds. Therefore it is not a command of God not to eat, but Moses spoke in spirit. Therefore he said concerning the pig: You will not be glued, he says, to such people, who are similar to pigs: that is when they squander, they forget the Lord, when they are in need, they recognize the Lord, just as the pig when it eats does not know the Lord, when it is hungry it cries out, and having eaten again it is silent. You will not eat the eagle nor the oxypecter nor the fish-weasel nor the crow: not, he says, you will be glued nor similar to such people, who do not know how to provide food for themselves through labor and sweat, but seize the things of others in their lawlessness and watch as they walk in uncleanness and look around to see whom they might strip through greed, just as these birds alone do not provide food for themselves, but sitting idly they seek how they might eat the flesh of others, being polluted by their wickedness. And you will not eat, he says, the smyrnian nor the polypod nor the cuttlefish: not, he says, you will be similar being glued to such people, who are ungodly and already judged to death, just as these little fish are alone cursed in the deep swimming, not swimming as the others, but dwelling on the ground below the deep. But also you will not eat the dasypus. Why? Not, he says, you will become a corrupter of children nor similar to such, because the hare each year oversteps its burrow: for as many years it lives, so many holes it has. But also you will not eat the hyena: not, he says, you will become an adulterer nor corrupter nor similar to such. Why? Because this animal changes its nature each year and sometimes is male, sometimes female. But also he hated the cat well. Not, he says, you will become such, who we hear committing lawlessness with the mouth through uncleanness, nor will you be glued to the unclean who commit lawlessness with the mouth. For this animal conceives with the mouth. Concerning foods Moses took three doctrines and thus spoke in spirit: but they according to the desire of the flesh as concerning eating received them. But David receives knowledge of the same three doctrines and says: Blessed is the man who did not walk in the counsel of the ungodly, just as the fish walk in darkness into the depths: and in the way of sinners he did not stand, just as those who seem to fear the Lord sin like the pig, and on the seat of the polluted he did not sit, just as the birds sitting for plunder. You have it completely concerning eating. Again Moses says: Eat every split and chewed thing. What does he say? That taking food he knows the one who nourishes him and resting on him seems to rejoice. He spoke well seeing the command. What then does he say? Be glued with those who fear the Lord, with those who meditate on what they received as a word of distinction in the heart, with those who speak the teachings of the Lord and keep them, with those who know that meditation is a work of joy, and who chew the word of the Lord. What is the split thing? That the righteous both walks in this world and awaits the holy age. See how Moses legislated well. But from where will they understand these things or comprehend? We however having understood the commands rightly speak, as the Lord willed. Therefore we circumcise our ears and hearts, so that we might comprehend these things.
pass_b_english: Moses said, 'Do not eat pig or eagle or oxypecter or crow or any fish that does not have scales in itself.' In doing so, he took three doctrines in wisdom. For he says to them in Deuteronomy (Deuteronomy): 'And I will make a covenant with this people, my righteous deeds.' Therefore, it is not a command of God not to eat, but Moses spoke in spirit. Moses said concerning the pig: 'You will not be like such people,' he says, 'who are similar to pigs - that is, when they have plenty, they forget the Lord, but when they are in need, they recognize the Lord, just as the pig, when it eats, does not know the Lord, but when it is hungry, it cries out, and having eaten again, it is silent.' You will not eat the eagle or the oxypecter or the fish-weasel or the crow: 'Not,' he says, 'you will be like such people, who do not know how to provide food for themselves through labor and sweat, but seize the things of others in their lawlessness and watch as they walk in uncleanness, looking around to see whom they might strip through greed, just as these birds alone do not provide food for themselves, but sitting idly, they seek how they might eat the flesh of others, being polluted by their wickedness.' And you will not eat, he says, the smyrnian or the polypod or the cuttlefish: 'Not,' he says, 'you will be like such people, who are ungodly and already judged to death, just as these little fish are alone cursed in the deep, swimming, not swimming as the others, but dwelling on the ground below the deep.' But also, you will not eat the dasypus. Why? 'Not,' he says, 'you will become a corrupter of children, nor be like such, because the hare each year oversteps its burrow - for as many years it lives, so many holes it has.' But also, you will not eat the hyena: 'Not,' he says, 'you will become an adulterer, nor a corrupter, nor be like such.' Why? Because this animal changes its nature each year and sometimes is male, sometimes female. But also, he hated the cat well. 'Not,' he says, 'you will become such, who we hear committing lawlessness with the mouth through uncleanness, nor will you be like the unclean who commit lawlessness with the mouth.' For this animal conceives with the mouth. Concerning foods, Moses took three doctrines and thus spoke in spirit: but they, according to the desire of the flesh, as concerning eating, received them. But David receives knowledge of the same three doctrines and says: 'Blessed is the man who did not walk in the counsel of the ungodly,' (Psalm 1:1) just as the fish walk in darkness into the depths, and in the way of sinners, he did not stand, just as those who seem to fear the Lord sin like the pig, and on the seat of the polluted, he did not sit, just as the birds sitting for plunder. You have it completely concerning eating. Again, Moses says: 'Eat every split and chewed thing.' What does he say? That taking food, he knows the one who nourishes him, and resting on him, seems to rejoice. He spoke well, seeing the command. What then does he say? 'Be like those who fear the Lord, with those who meditate on what they received as a word of distinction in the heart, with those who speak the teachings of the Lord and keep them, with those who know that meditation is a work of joy, and who chew the word of the Lord.' What is the split thing? That the righteous both walks in this world and awaits the holy age. See how Moses legislated well. But from where will they understand these things or comprehend? We, however, having understood the commands rightly, speak as the Lord willed. Therefore, we circumcise our ears and hearts, so that we might comprehend these things.
